html:
Ali Abdullah Saleh was the president of North Yemen from 1978 and of united Yemen from 1990 until 2012. He described ruling Yemen as dancing on the heads of snakes.

An army officer, he came to power after two presidents were murdered in a year. He kept power by balancing tribes, the army, Islamists and foreign patrons, and led the north into unification in 1990. He won the 1994 war against the southern secession.

Protests of the Arab Spring in 2011 forced him out under a Gulf-brokered deal. He then allied with the Houthis, his old enemies, helping them take Sana'a in 2014. When he switched sides again in December 2017, they killed him. See Yemeni civil war.
sum: Ali Abdullah Saleh was the president of North Yemen from 1978 and of united Yemen from 1990 until 2012. He described ruling Yemen as dancing on the heads of snakes.
